findings.description: Discrimination half, R10: reverting the relaxation to strict adjacency by hand turns exactly the new M7 case red, and nothing else — the linter goes silent (rc 4 to rc 0) on the same input.
findings.evidence: Copied the tree to a tmpdir, replaced `_governs_plural_noun` with the strict pre-job body (only the token immediately after the number), ran the suite: `FAIL M7 count separated from its noun by an adjective: exit 4 (heuristic)  rc=0 err=` / `FAIL M7: R10 named  err=''` / `211 passed, 2 failed`. Unmutated control in the same tree: `213 passed, 0 failed`.

findings.description: Discrimination half, R21: stubbing `rule_R21` to return None turns exactly the new R21 case red, all four of its assertions, and nothing else.
findings.evidence: Spliced `def rule_R21(*a, **k): return None` above the last `__main__` guard in a tree copy, ran the suite: `FAIL R21 deterministic task citing a rubric clause: exit 1 (proof)  rc=0 err=` plus `R21: R21 named`, `R21: task named`, `R21: offending clause named`; `209 passed, 4 failed`.

findings.description: Discrimination half, R2: stripping the anchor's own text out of `r2_anchor_message` by value while leaving every line number it reports intact turns exactly one case red — the new R2-anchor case — while every older R2 case stays green, which is the precise property C-9 asks for.
findings.evidence: Wrapped `r2_anchor_message` above the last `__main__` guard to replace both `repr(anchor)` and `str(anchor)` with `<stripped>`; suite went `213 passed, 0 failed` to `212 passed, 1 failed`, the single failure being `FAIL R2-anchor: anchor text itself quoted in the diagnostic, not just its line numbers  err="job-spec: [heuristic] R2 citation-anchor: tasks/T-001.md:57 cites .agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py:58 quoting <stripped>, which sits on this same line (tasks/T-001.md:57)..."`. Note every number survived the strip and only the quoted anchor went missing.

findings.description: The probe designated by the clause's check agrees, reporting all four mutations red with their liveness lines green, so no coverage mutation was skipped unmeasured.
findings.evidence: `python3 .agent-guild/state/checks/probe.py suite-coverage` exit 0: `ok the suite is not skipping its corpus cases`, `ok R10 adjacency: mutation landed` / `disabling it turns the suite red`, `ok R21 checker routing: mutation landed` / `disabling it turns the suite red`, `ok R2 diagnostic: r2_anchor_message exists as the seam` / `wrapper spliced above the entry guard` / `the wrapper actually strips the anchor at runtime` / `removing the quoted anchor turns the suite red`, `ok R10 relaxation: _governs_plural_noun is still the predicate` / `revert to strict adjacency landed` / `the old strict behavior turns the suite red`. No seam finding: `r2_anchor_message(anchor, label, src_line, path, lineno, actual_line, anchor_line)` at check-job-spec.py:937 names the parameter `anchor` as the clause requires.

findings.description: Archive-drawn half: all three cases mutate one line of real shipped paperwork from the tracked #117 corpus, and I confirmed each source string exists verbatim in the archived file rather than in an invented fixture.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD -- .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py` shows +83/-0, every case built on `copy_corpus_state`, whose `ARCHIVE_DIR` is `_corpus.ARCHIVE_117` = `.agent-guild/state/archive/2026-08-10-issue-117` (_corpus.py:21-23). Sources confirmed in the archive: M7 mutates `record three findings` at archive/2026-08-10-issue-117/tasks/T-006.md:41; R21 mutates `checker: checker-judgment` at .../tasks/T-001.md:8 on a task whose `clauses: [C-2, C-7]` (line 5) are both `checker-judgment:` rubrics in the archived constitution (lines 32, 62); R2-anchor mutates `.agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py:64` at .../tasks/T-001.md:57. `mutate()` asserts count==1 on each, and all three `mutation string found exactly once` assertions pass. No hand-written constitution anywhere in the added cases.

findings.description: The R21 shape is reachable only by mutating a real task's `checker:` line, which the clause and spec both name as correct rather than synthetic, and I re-derived the resulting diagnostic straight from the archive myself.
findings.evidence: Ran check-job-spec.py over a fresh copy of the archived #117 state with only that one line changed: `job-spec: [proof] R21 checker-routing: tasks/T-001.md declares checker: checker-deterministic but cites C-2, whose constitution check is checker-judgment:—that agent runs scripts and exercises no judgment, so the rubric can't be applied`, rc=1. Matches the case's assertions on task id and clause id.

findings.description: The R2 case asserts the anchor text itself, not merely that R2 fired, and I confirmed the asserted string is genuinely the quoted anchor in the live diagnostic rather than an incidental substring.
findings.evidence: Case asserts `"val[0] == val[-1]" in err` (test_check_job_spec.py, R2-anchor block). Re-derived diagnostic from the archive: `R2 citation-anchor: tasks/T-001.md:57 cites .agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py:58 quoting 'if len(val) >= 2 and val[0] == val[-1] and val[0] in "\\"'"', which sits on this same line (tasks/T-001.md:57) in the citing document—but that code is actually at .agent-guild/scripts/compose-brief.py:64`. The asserted span sits inside the quoted anchor, and the strip test above proves it vanishes with the anchor.

findings.description: Exit codes match the rule classes: R2 and R10 are heuristics asserted at 4, R21 is a proof asserted at 1, and my own reproduction returns those same codes.
findings.evidence: Case assertions: `M7 count separated from its noun by an adjective: exit 4 (heuristic)` rc==4, `R2-anchor stale code citation: exit 4 (heuristic)` rc==4, `R21 deterministic task citing a rubric clause: exit 1 (proof)` rc==1. Independent reproduction from the archive returned rc=4 (R2-anchor, with the `[heuristic]` tag and lint-exception footer), rc=4 (M7, same), rc=1 (R21, `[proof]`).

findings.description: The suite passes as delivered, and the change is purely additive, so no pre-existing case was weakened to make room for the new ones.
findings.evidence: `python3 .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py` → `230 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0. All 15 new-case assertions green (M7 x4, R21 x5, R2-anchor x5, plus the three `mutation string found exactly once` guards). `git diff HEAD --numstat` → `83	0	.agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py`.

findings.description: Scope is clean: T-002 modified only its own artifact and committed nothing, so C-7's working-tree reads still have something to inspect.
findings.evidence: `git status --porcelain` → ` M .agent-guild/scripts/check-job-spec.py` and ` M .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py` only; the former is T-001's delivered artifact, not a T-002 scope violation. `git log --oneline ae3f757..HEAD | wc -l` → 0, so nothing was committed.
